**RE: Urgent Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial**
*   **Member Name:** Harper Alvarez
*   **Member ID:** W597643658
*   **Reference Number:** POC-5ED3BAB6CA-81537
*   **Requested Service:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030)
*   **Ordering Provider:** Dr. [First Name] Duval, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)
*   **Date of Denial Notice:** August 6, 2026

Dear Appeals Review Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of the prior authorization request for a lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT code 63030) scheduled to be performed by Dr. Duval, MD. The denial letter dated August 6, 2026, states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." 

This determination is medically incorrect and directly contradicted by my clinical records. I have completed multiple rounds of extensive, supervised, and invasive conservative treatments over the last two years, all of which have failed to resolve my debilitating pain and neurological symptoms. 

Below, I map my documented medical history directly to the clinical necessity requirements to demonstrate that my trial of conservative treatment has been more than adequate.

### 1. Documented Conservative Treatment History

My medical records outline three distinct modalities of conservative therapy that have been exhausted without lasting relief:

*   **Supervised Physical Therapy (10 Weeks, 16 Visits):** From April 24, 2026, to July 3, 2026, I actively participated in and completed 16 sessions of a structured, professionally supervised physical therapy program. This program focused specifically on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility. Despite full compliance, my symptoms remained progressive and severe. This trial is fully documented in the attached physical therapy discharge note.
*   **Oral Pharmacotherapy (8 Months):** I completed an 8-month trial of oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) to manage my lower back pain. This long-term medication trial failed to provide adequate functional or pain relief.
*   **Interventional Therapy / Corticosteroid Injection:** On April 21, 2026, I underwent a lumbar corticosteroid injection. This interventional procedure provided only temporary, partial relief that lasted for 4 weeks before my severe symptoms fully returned.

### 2. Clinical Findings and Objective Pathology

My ongoing symptoms are severe, progressive, and clearly correlate with severe, objective spinal pathology:

*   **Symptom Duration and Severity:** I have suffered from 24 months of progressive pain in my lower back that is completely unrelieved by rest. 
*   **Severe Functional Limitation:** Due to severe radicular pain radiating into my right calf, I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.
*   **Objective Clinical Examination:** Physical examinations performed by Dr. Duval document positive provocative testing on my right side and a neurological deficit that corresponds directly to the L4-L5 level.
*   **Diagnostic Imaging Support:** An MRI of my lumbar spine, dated June 24, 2026, objectively confirms an "L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root." This imaging perfectly explains my right-sided radicular pain and neurological deficit.
*   **Surgical Candidacy:** I am an excellent candidate for this decompression procedure. I have a BMI of 29, am a non-smoker, have no active infections, and have no untreated substance use disorders.

### 3. Alignment with State Medicaid Medical Policies

Depending on the specific plan administrator reviewing this appeal, my clinical presentation exceeds all relevant medical policy thresholds:

*   Under the Humana Medicaid Medical Coverage Policy for **"Spinal Decompression Surgery"** (Policy Number: **HUM-SC-2660-000**, Effective Date: **07/22/2026**), a member is eligible for decompression/discectomy for a herniated disc confirmed by imaging when accompanied by:
    > "Radicular* pain that has persisted despite 6 weeks of at least one of the following conservative treatments1,32,33: 
    > ▪ Epidural steroid injections or facet joint/medial branch nerve blocks if medically appropriate and not contraindicated1,33; OR 
    > ▪ Medications (eg, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDs], non-narcotic analgesics) if medically appropriate and not contraindicated1; OR 
    > ▪ Physical therapy (PT)1,33"

    My records document that I have completed **all three** of these options: 10 weeks of physical therapy (exceeding the 6-week standard), 8 months of NSAID medications (exceeding the 6-week standard), and a corticosteroid injection. My radicular pain has persisted for 24 months, vastly exceeding the plan's 6-week duration guideline.

*   To the extent that UnitedHealthcare Community Plan or other Kentucky Medicaid administrators utilize proprietary InterQual® criteria (such as **"InterQual® CP: Procedures: Decompression +/- Fusion, Lumbar"**), please note that those guidelines have not been directly quoted here as they are proprietary. However, standard clinical guidelines across all administrators recognize that a 10-week course of physical therapy, an 8-month course of NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection satisfy any clinical requirement for an "adequate trial of conservative treatment."

### Conclusion

The clinical evidence attached to this appeal overwhelmingly documents that my conservative care has been robust, compliant, and thoroughly exhausted over a multi-month and multi-year period. Denying coverage for this decompression surgery when my functional capacity is limited to less than 10 minutes of standing is a severe threat to my health and daily function.

Please review the attached physical therapy discharge summary, MRI report dated June 24, 2026, and Dr. Duval's clinical notes, and reverse this adverse determination immediately.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Harper Alvarez
Member ID: W597643658

1. Dr. Duval, MD - Orthopedic Surgery Clinical Evaluation Notes
2. Lumbar Spine MRI Report (dated June 24, 2026)
3. Physical Therapy Discharge Summary (showing 16 visits, 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03)
4. Record of Lumbar Corticosteroid Injection (dated April 21, 2026)
